name: district_heating_loop
title: District heating loop (consumer, feed pump, pipes with pressure drop and heat loss)
summary: Small district-heating loop (TESPy basic tutorial): heating plant, feed pump with isentropic efficiency, consumer with 2 % pressure drop, isenthalpic control valve and two pipes with Darcy-Weisbach pressure drop (Colebrook-White) and UA*LMTD heat loss to the ambient; returns the mass flow, the pump power, the heat duties and the loop efficiency, and reproduces the tutorial's part-load studies.

authors: Francesco Witte (TESPy lead developer) and the TESPy contributors
origin.course: TESPy basic tutorial District Heating Network (commit 19425523)

verification.summary: Compared with a re-run of the TESPy tutorial district_heating.py: 20 common variables, max relative deviation 3.65e-03 on m_dot (INCOMP::Water vs Water properties); in the sweeps efficiency agrees to 3.6e-07 and pipe heat loss to 2.8e-06. The loop energy balance closes (-3.4e-9 W).
verification.reference: TESPy tutorial district_heating.py re-run from the local snapshot (commit 19425523) in a throw-away venv (Python 3.12, TESPy 0.11.3.dev0, CoolProp 8.0.0): base case (sec_4/sec_5) and two points of each of the three part-load sweeps (sec_5); the loop energy balance of the script is compared as well
verification.notes: Base case: 20 common variables, max relative deviation 3.65e-03 (m_dot); W_pump 1.0e-03, dp_valve 7.8e-04, pressures <= 8.3e-05, temperatures <= 1.3e-05, eta 7.0e-08. Caused by the fluid properties: TESPy uses CoolProp's incompressible back end INCOMP::Water (rho 968.3 kg/m3, cp 4189 J/kg-K at 90 degC), the model the real EES fluid Water (rho 965.7 kg/m3, cp 4203 J/kg-K). Absolute enthalpies h[i] are not compared (reference-state offset: TESPy h=0 at 0 K, CoolProp Water IIR h=200 kJ/kg at 0 degC); the enthalpy differences enter through the compared duties. Sweep points: eta agrees to 3.6e-07, pipe heat loss to 2.8e-06, m_dot to 3.65e-03. Energy balance Q_hs + W_pump + Q_cons + Q_feed + Q_return = -3.4e-9 W.
